waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: East-side approach — NOT Blue Lake TH. The Hairpin is the start point.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the hairpin turn and pond pullout on the east side of Washington Pass, at about 5,100 ft, and park there. Make sure that is the pullout you actually want, because two trailheads on opposite sides of the pass serve this same summit: the Blue Lake Trailhead, roughly 2.5 miles away by road on the far side of the pass, is for the west-side routes and not for this one, and getting that wrong costs you an hour. The season here runs about June through September. There is no water on the approach, so carry what you need from the car.

waypoints.name: Base of Flycatcher Buttress
waypoints.note: Stay right of the gully dividing the two spires, scrambling to a flat ledge at the start.
waypoints.directions: Hike up from the hairpin into the Spire Gully, following occasional cairns to the last large tree in the center of the gully, then traverse right across talus (snow early season) toward the gully that runs up to the notch between the two Early Winters Spires. Stay right of that dividing gully and scramble to the flat ledge at the start of the route.

waypoints.name: North Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Climb the ten pitches of the buttress (5.10b), taking the left of the two cracks on the pitch-6 crux and traversing left rather than going straight up off the pitch-8 belay; easy ground then leads to the summit plateau and the top.
